The '''1983 Copa de la Liga''' was the first edition of [[Copa de la Liga]]. The competition started on May 8, 1983, and concluded on June 29, 1983. Due to time constraints, saturation and club pressure, the [[Copa de la Liga]] only lasted four years since 1982, being cancelled in 1986.<ref>[https://www.rsssf.org/tabless/spanleagcuphist.html Spain - List of League Cup Finals] on the RSSSF</ref>

==Format==
The Copa de la Liga was played by 18 teams of [[1982–83 La Liga]]. All rounds are played over [[two-legged tie|two legs]]. The team that has the higher aggregate score over the two legs progresses to the next round. The [[1982–83 Copa del Rey]] semifinal losers are exempt until second round, and the [[1982–83 Copa del Rey]] final teams are exempt until quarterfinals.

==First round==
First leg: 8 May 1983. Second leg: 21 and 22 May 1983.

{{TwoLegStart}}
{{TwoLegResult|[[Celta de Vigo]] || 4–9 |'''[[RCD Espanyol|RCD Español]]'''|| 3–2 | 1–7 |winner=2}}

{{TwoLegResult|'''[[Racing Santander]]'''|| 4–3 |[[Valencia CF]]|| 1–0 | 3–3 |winner=1}}
{{TwoLegResult|[[UD Salamanca]] || 1–4 |'''[[Atlético Madrid]]'''|| 0–0 | 1–4 |winner=2}}
{{TwoLegResult|'''[[Real Zaragoza]]'''|| 4–1 |[[Sevilla FC]] || 2–1 | 2–0 |winner=1}}

==Second round==
First leg: June 1, 1983. Second leg: June 8, 1983.
{{TwoLegStart}}
{{TwoLegResult|'''[[Atlético Madrid]]'''|| 3–2 |[[Athletic Bilbao]]|| 3–0 | 0–2 |winner=1}}
{{TwoLegResult|'''[[Sporting Gijón]]'''|| 3–2 | [[Málaga CF]]|| 2–2 | 1–0 |winner=1}}
{{TwoLegResult|[[Racing Santander]]|| 3–6 |'''[[Real Zaragoza]]'''|| 3–2 | 0–4 |winner=2}}
{{TwoLegResult|'''[[Real Sociedad]]'''|| ([[Penalty kick (association football)|p]]) 2–2 | [[RCD Espanyol|RCD Español]] || 2–2 | 0–0 |winner=1}}
|}
*Bye: [[UD Las Palmas]].

== Quarter-finals ==
First leg: June 12, 1983. Second leg: June 15, 1983.
{{TwoLegStart}}
{{TwoLegResult|'''[[Real Madrid]]'''|| 2–1 | [[Real Sociedad]] || 1–0 | 1–1 |winner=1}}
{{TwoLegResult|'''[[FC Barcelona]]'''|| 1–0 | [[Sporting Gijón]] || 1–0 | 0–0 |winner=1}}
{{TwoLegResult|[[UD Las Palmas]] || 1–3 |'''[[Atlético Madrid]]'''|| 1–0 | 0–3 |winner=2}}
|}
*Bye: [[Real Zaragoza]].

==Semi-finals==
First leg: June 19, 1983. Second leg: June 22, 1983.
